..
A couple of prominent features have led to the inclusion of 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms for tonight. An upper- 
level low is centered W of Guam, and is expected to remain quasi- 
stationary, keeping upper-level divergence favorable for convection 
at least through tonight. A weak trade-wind trough extending from the
SE will continue its westward motion. However, incoming Precipitable
Water (PWAT) values of 2.0 inches and the previously mentioned 
upper-level low will keep the Marianas in a convectively-prone 
weather pattern. As for Monday, the relatively dry trade-wind regime 
will continue, with island heating leading to showers building up 
over leeward portions of the islands before being advected offshore 
by the trade winds. Invest 92W is of sub-low status according to 
JTWC. Consequently, forecaster confidence is low regarding potential 
impacts to the Marianas in the latter half of the week. Therefore, 
Probability of Precipitation (POP) will remain at 30 percent until 
there is increased certainty regarding Invest 92W (refer to the 
Tropical Systems section below).

Marine...
Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms will be the main threat
for coastal waters and shorelines tonight. Light to gentle east to 
northeast winds and combined seas around 3 ft are expected through 
Monday night. Starting Monday afternoon, island heating during the 
daytime will lead to increased showers over western coastal waters 
through early Monday evening. A pulse in east swell may increase
combined seas by a foot or two starting on Tuesday.

Tropical Systems...
Joint Typhoon Warning Center's Invest 92W is centered west of Majuro
near 7.2N 168.9E, moving WNW. Invest 92W is still sub-low, meaning 
development is not expected for at least the next couple of days. 
92W remains poorly organized, with most of the convection associated 
with it seen to the north of the center. Latest model guidance has 
slowed down and backed off a bit on development of 92W, with the 
possible genesis area now much farther northwest. Models differ 
significantly on the track and development of 92W as it continues to 
move west-northwest, with the GFS being the most aggressive and the 
ECMWF being the least aggressive. Invest 92W will continue to be 
monitored closely over the next few days for any indications that it 
will begin to organize and strengthen.

Eastern Micronesia...
The Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) and Invest 92W remain the primary
weather producers across eastern Micronesia. Invest 92W remains
poorly organized and most of the convection is now seen north of the
center in a band of enhanced convergence north of 10N. The NET is
lacking any convection as well, except well south of the trough. As
92W continues to move west-northwest, it is still expected to pull
the NET along with it, bringing increased convection to Pohnpei and
Kosrae later in the week. As the NET and 92W move out of the
Marshalls, Majuro is likely to see showers bouncing between isolated
and scattered. Invest 92W is fairly unimpressive right now, resulting
in less convection than previous forecasts were predicting. Marine
conditions look to remain fairly benign, with light to gentle winds
and seas at or below 5 feet.

Western Micronesia...
A quiet doldrum-like pattern persists across the region. The Near- 
Equatorial Trough extends eastward across nearly all of Micronesia, 
but is convectively very quiet until it reaches as far east as the 
Marshall Islands. There is a broad upper-level low just north of 
western Micronesia, centered between Yap Proper and the Marianas, but
it is providing very little in the way of convective upper-level 
support. Himawari visible satellite imagery reveals some island- 
effect showers over the larger islands of Palau this afternoon, 
supported by a very light and variable wind field as indicated by 
surface observations and scatterometry. Similar conditions are 
expected for the next few days, and afternoon island-effect showers 
were included in the forecast for Monday and Tuesday. For Yap, 
isolated showers, partly cloudy skies, and light northeast to east 
winds are expected throughout the period. Chuuk remains in a quiet 
pattern as well, but can expect increasing showers in the latter half
of the week as models depict Invest 92W passing north of Weno, with 
an area of increased convergence in its wake.

Benign sea conditions are expected to continue. Latest altimetry 
shows combined seas between 2 and 4 feet across the region. Palau and
Yap will continue to see a primary northeast to east swell 
throughout the week. Primary swell is southeast across Chuuk, with a 
light secondary swell out of the east-northeast.
